episodes.181008: Daytime heating and a surface boundary led to scattered showers and thunderstorms developing, an isolated one or two reached severe limits.
episodes.181070: A subltle shortwave trough within northwest flow moved across the region and provided enought lift for scattered afternoon thunderstorms. There was sufficient MLCAPE (1500 J/kg) and Effective Shear (30kts) for some stronger updrafts that produced severe hail and damaging wind gusts. Overall these storms were relatively short lived and died off once the outflow undercut the updraft. |Of particular note, in Elk River a tree feel on a tent where there was a birthday party ongoing. There were 3 minor injuries.
episodes.181072: A cold front brought showers and thunderstorms across the region which resulted in severe weather and flash flooding.  The backbuilding nature of the storms resulted in localized flash flooding in Hillsborough County. Add detail for svr....
episodes.181078: Scattered severe t-storms during the afternoon on July 22nd produced a brief small land spout type tornado and numerous large hail reports.
episodes.181080: Northwest flow rounding the northeastern periphery of an upper high over AZ combined with abundant low-level moisture over the high plains of eastern NM to produce severe weather along and east of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains on July 21st and 22nd. Large hail and severe winds were observed from these scattered storm cells. Heavy rainfall also produced flash flooding on the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar on July 21st. Fast flowing flood waters with burn scar debris was observed at several locations causing damage to properties and forcing two road closures north and south of Mora, NM. Flash flooding was also reported near the Ute Park burn scar along the Ponil Creek.
episodes.181109: A subltle shortwave trough within northwest flow moved across the region and provided enought lift for scattered afternoon thunderstorms. There was sufficient MLCAPE (1500 J/kg) and Effective Shear (30kts) for some stronger updrafts that produced severe hail and damaging wind gusts. Overall these storms were relatively short lived and died off once the outflow undercut the updraft.
episodes.181156: Isolated strong thunderstorms produced gusty outflow winds across Nevada.
episodes.181163: Thunderstorms over eastern White Pine county produced gusty winds.
episodes.181186: A large upper level ridge of high pressure over the Rockies and Southern Plains began to retreat west of the Four State Region on July 22nd, as a weak upper level disturbance shifted southeast into the region and Lower Mississippi Valley. This disturbance reinforced a weak cool front south through the area, and focused scattered showers and thunderstorms during the mid and late afternoon hours over portions of Deep East Texas and Central Louisiana during peak heating. This heating and the available low level moisture in place contributed to strong instability which enhanced this thunderstorm development, contributing to a couple of these storms becoming briefly severe. One severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in the Ebarb community in Western Sabine Parish before weakening as it moved into Vernon Parish late in the afternoon.
episodes.181386: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard Coast and a waterspout along the Volusia Coast.
episodes.181388: Thunderstorms produced a landspout tornado in Volusia County and a severe wind gust in Brevard County.
episodes.181751: Thunderstorms developed along the lake breeze around midday along the Lake Michigan shoreline. These storms produced hail up to half dollar size.  Another round of thunderstorms developed across northeast Wisconsin during the late afternoon and early evening hours.  These storms produced damaging winds and small hail.
episodes.181893: A weak surface trough and upper level disturbance led to rounds of strong thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Some hail and damaging winds were observed.
episodes.181968: A late night gust front from a thunderstorm complex across south Georgia moved offshore and produced wind gust of 40-45 mph along the local NE FL Atlantic coast as it moved offshore.
episodes.181969: A wavering surface boundary across SE Georgia, the dominant Gulf Coast sea breeze and steep mid and upper-level lapse rates combined with some dry pockets of low-level air produced scattered diurnally enhanced strong to severe storms that produced wind gusts of 40-60 mph.
episodes.181970: A wavering surface boundary across SE Georgia, the dominant Gulf Coast sea breeze and steep mid and upper-level lapse rates combined with some dry pockets of low-level air produced scattered diurnally enhanced strong to severe storms that produced wind gusts of 40-60 mph.
episodes.182016: A warm front stalled across Connecticut and Rhode Island, producing thunderstorms with very heavy rainfall.  This caused significant flash flooding.  Also, wind shear was just strong enough for a few thunderstorms to become severe, with locally damaging wind gusts.  A Tornado Warning was even issued for a storm in northern Worcester County, but no tornado damage was reported.
episodes.182196: A thunderstorm was occasionally severe as it tracked southeastward across the northeastern and eastern foothills of the Black Hills. The storm produced hail larger than golf ball size.
episodes.182197: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over eastern Todd County, producing wind gusts to 60 mph.
episodes.182274: Nebraska was on the backside of an upper trough. A weak shortwave trough moved over the Central Plains and resulted in an increase in atmospheric lift. Most unstable CAPE was around 3,000 J/kg and effective bulk shear was around 35 knots. Mid-level lapse rates were around 7 degrees C/km. Temperatures were between 85 and 90 degrees across south central Nebraska. Dewpoint temperatures were between 60 and 65 degrees. ||A storm strengthened over Gosper County and moved into Furnas County and produced nickel sized hail at 2:44 PM CDT. This storm went on to produce two inch hail in Furnas County. Additional storms developed across south central Nebraska and produced large hail during the afternoon and early evening hours of July 22nd. The largest hail of 2.50 inches occurred in Buffalo and Phelps Counties. The storms ended by producing nickel size hail in Clay County at 6:40 PM CDT.
episodes.182955: In the afternoon of the 22nd, discrete supercells formed in southwest Nebraska. These cells produced hail of over four inches in diameter.
episodes.182956: In the afternoon of the 22nd, multiple supercells formed across eastern Colorado, southwestern Nebraska, and northwestern Kansas. These storms produced a wind gust over 70 mph and larger than 2 inch hail.
episodes.182993: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.182999: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.183004: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms occurred within a favorable environment for downbursts.  Several reports of damaging winds were received.
episodes.183130: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved across much of north and central GA during the afternoon and evening hours of July 21st. Numerous reports of damaging winds, along with significant flash flooding (around downtown Atlanta) occurred along the I-20 corridor. Another area impacted by damaging winds occurred from Stewart County (far SE part of the FFC forecast area) to near Swainsboro in Emanuel County.
episodes.183134: A potent shortwave diving south out of Manitoba kicked off storms that produced large hail across parts of the region. One storm during the early afternoon produced tennis ball size hail denting vehicles on Highway 38 in northern Itasca County. This storm continued to move to the south and moved through the Grand Rapids area periodically dropping hail stones an inch in diameter. Other storms that afternoon across the Minnesota Arrowhead produced quarter-sized hail in Tettegouche State Park.
episodes.183180: Moist, convergent flow over the Atlantic waters lead to the development of a band of showers along the coast of Palm Beach County on the afternoon of July 22nd. Additional strong thunderstorms moved over Lake Okeechobee during the afternoon.
episodes.183328: A weak cold front drifted into the region while a trough dug south to the gulf. Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed with some becoming severe.
episodes.183464: A lone supercell moved south across the central Sandhills during the late evening of July 21, producing large hail in Blaine County.
episodes.183465: Scattered supercells moved south from the Sandhills into southwest Nebraska throughout the afternoon and evening of July 22. Multiple reports of large hail and severe winds were received across several counties.
episodes.183596: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Severe thunderstorm outflow gusts occurred in Graham and Greenlee counties and some tree damage occurred in Tucson.
episodes.183693: In the evening hours of 7/21, strong thunderstorms moved across southeast Georgia and produced strong wind gusts along the Georgia coast and the adjacent coastal waters in the late evening and into the early morning hours of 7/22. Another round of thunderstorms impacted portions of the Georgia coast and the coastal waters in the afternoon of 7/22.
episodes.183780: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts across portions of Adams, Denver, Elbert, Lincoln and Logan Counties.  The hail ranged in size from 1 to 2 inches in diameter.  Peak wind gusts up to around 70 mph were observed.  In Logan County, a spotter reported significant crop damage at their location.  The storms also caused tree damage as well as property damage to homes and vehicles.  In Elbert County, a greenhouse sustained damage and several chickens were killed.  In Lincoln County,  significant hail and wind damage was reported between Genoa and Arriba.   Several semi-trailers were flipped.  Several power poles also were also knocked down near the intersection of county roads 42 and 3P.  Heavy rain produced localized flash flooding in the Cameron Peak burn scar north of Glen Haven.
episodes.183782: A severe thunderstorm in Weld County produced large hail, up to half dollar size.
episodes.183815: An upper impulse tracked southeast in a northwest flow pattern and produced scattered to numerous thunderstorms across north Alabama during the peak heating of the day, some severe with damaging winds.
episodes.183827: Despite less than 1000 J/kg MLCAPE and less than 30 knots deep-layer shear, a few storms managed to produce brief marginally large hail.
episodes.183829: An isolated storm along a frontal boundary produced a local burst of damaging wind.
episodes.183831: Limited instability and shear led to rapidly developing and dissipating storms. The strongest storms briefly produced large hail, with some very large observed in southeast South Dakota near Salem.
episodes.183832: Limited instability and shear led to rapidly developing and dissipating storms. The strongest storms briefly produced large hail.
episodes.183916: A surface trough was located along the Rio Grande Valley with southeast surface winds bringing in modest moisture to the Sacramento Mountains. A weak disturbance moving through northwest flow aloft provided enough lift for a strong thunderstorm to drop hail up to the size of pennies near Cloudcroft.
episodes.183944: An outflow boundary moved through Cody and brought strong wind. A 61 mph wind gust occurred at the Cody airport.
episodes.184081: A remnant outflow boundary made its way over southern Mississippi during the morning. Once daytime heating increased, convection formed along that boundary. The convection formed a line and surged out across southeast Louisiana, coastal Mississippi, and the marine waters before dying out at sunset.
episodes.184083: A remnant outflow boundary made its way over southern Mississippi during the morning. Once daytime heating increased, convection formed along that boundary. The convection formed a line and surged out across southeast Louisiana, coastal Mississippi, and the marine waters before dying out at sunset.
episodes.184122: An upper level trough slowly moved through aloft as a cold front passed over the waters at the surface. A cluster of severe thunderstorms developed and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184190: Scattered thunderstorms formed over northwest lower Michigan as a weak troughing overspread an unstable airmass in place. A few storms produced severe hail, specifically over Grand Traverse and Wexford counties.
episodes.184313: Strong thunderstorms produced large hail in southwest Alabama.
episodes.184314: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced strong winds.
episodes.184377: A cluster of storms moved through the Upper Mississippi River Valley during the evening hours of July 22nd. The line of storms spanned from Mower to Houston County with stronger storms along the western portion of the line. Resultant large to very large hail was recorded in Dodge, Olmsted, and Mower counties. The largest hail recorded was ping pong ball size in Rochester (Olmsted County) and near Grand Meadow (Mower County).
episodes.184387: An upper level high pressure center was located over central Arizona and central New Mexico which resulted in a favorable pattern for efficient diurnal wind fluctuations including upslope oriented winds towards WFO Pueblo's eastern mountains. Weak waves embedded in the upper level northwesterly flow enhanced the lift and the pattern enhanced the deep shear. The result was a very rare mountainous tornado that was observed at around 9,000 feet.
episodes.184877: Isolated to widely scattered strong to severe thunderstorms impacted the coastal waters south of Cape Lookout on the morning of the 22nd.
episodes.185242: Scatter afternoon storms developed and a few were strong to severe.
